 KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 Pakistan beat India by four wickets, chasing 88 in just 3.5 overs at Hong Kong Sixes.
 Abbas Afridi hit five consecutive sixes off Krunal Pandya's first over, which cost 31 runs.
 Fans criticised Pandya and Nitish Rana, who made 19 off 14 balls, on social media.

 Bowled for golden duck, hit for 5 sixes: Krunal Pandya suffers nightmare outing against Pakistan in Hong Kong Sixes
 Abbas Afridi's blistering assault on Krunal Pandya turned the India vs Pakistan clash at the Hong Kong Sixes 2026 into a lopsided contest, and supporters have wasted little time in directing their anger at the Indian captain and at Nitish Rana.
 Pakistan, the defending champions, chased down their target in only 3.5 overs, and the margin was four wickets at the end of a Group C match played on Friday.
 India had been asked to bat first and could manage only 88 for five in their six overs. Shashank Singh was the one batter who looked comfortable, as he top-scored with an explosive 40 off 11 balls, but the rest of the line-up never found a rhythm, and the total proved far too small on a ground with such short boundaries.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pakistan had lost their opening game against the UAE by a wicket earlier in the tournament, so they were under pressure to win, and they started their reply with a point to prove. And the captain bore the brunt of it.
 The chase was effectively decided in its first over, since Pandya took the new ball and Afridi launched a ferocious attack on him. The right-hander hit five consecutive sixes, which brought 30 runs off the bat, and Khawaja Nafay added a single to make it 31 from the over.
 Afridi carried on against T Natarajan in the second over, adding a four and a six, and Pakistan raced to 59 without loss after only two overs. Nafay also hit boundaries of his own, so India never had a chance to build any pressure.
 Afridi's innings ended in the third over when he was caught by Natarajan off Shashank Singh for 35 off eight balls. Nafay stayed at the crease and scored 41 off 12 deliveries before Rahul Tewatia dismissed him in the fourth over. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MORE:  India and Pakistan avoid handshakes again as PAK beat IND convincingly at Hong Kong Super Sixes 
 Fans slam Krunal Pandya and Nitish Rana on social media
 Reaction on X was swift and mostly critical, and the first post came from a user who linked Krunal's performance to a recent storyline involving his brother.
 The user, @venomous1406, joked that Hardik Pandya had been in the news everywhere due to IPL trade rumours, so Krunal had taken his chance to enter the limelight as well.
 "Hardik Pandya was in the news everywhere. So, his brother Krunal took his chance to get himself in the limelight too," the post read, along with the hashtags #HongKongSixes2026 and #INDvsPAK.
 Another account listed what it called a nightmare outing for the Indian captain as @yogeshgoswami_ wrote: "MEET KRUNAL PANDYA - A NIGHTMARE OUTING! 😭💔 0 (1) with the bat. Conceded 31 runs in a single over, including five sixes! Lost to Pakistan as captain! A golden duck & a brutal hammering with the ball in Hongkong Sixes!"
 A third user concentrated on the number that mattered most as @crickrate posted: "31 runs in the first over of KRUNAL PANDYA. 😱 Totally destroyed by Abbas Afridi. 🔥"
 Some supporters criticised the captain's decision to bowl the first over himself, and @Vedantp13 was one of them. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Don't forget overconfident, self obsessed captain Krunal Pandya.... On a surface where pacers are bowling well & pak pacers got some help too. Oversmart Krunal Pandya came to bowl first over giving out 31 runs & it was game over for India right there," the post said.
 Rana scored 19 off 14 balls before retiring out and the batsman drew his own share of criticism for his innings.
 @AKSHAYKAPUR1982 was blunt in the assessment, calling him the "Biggest fraud nitish rana ..test match inings".
 While @CharlieGulshan criticised the lack of urgency and wrote: "Nitish Rana 19 off 14 in Hong Kong Sixes. Imagine you can't score runs when you have six fielders and outfield is quick. Sharm aani chahiye (Should be ashamed)."
 Why India's Hong Kong Sixes defeat was about decisions as much as hitting
 Afridi's five sixes will rightly be remembered as the highlight of the match, but the defeat also owed something to the choices made by India's leadership. A captain who opens the bowling in a format with six overs and tiny boundaries is taking a large risk, and when it fails the damage is almost impossible to undo.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Fans have been understandably harsh, although some of the criticism has gone beyond what the facts support. Pandya's first over was a disaster, yet one expensive over doesn't prove a lack of ability, and in a game where any bowler can be hit for six with relative ease, a plan that goes wrong can look much worse than it is.
 Rana's innings raises a different question. In a tournament where runs come thick and fast, a score of 19 from 14 balls is a slow return, and the decision to retire out showed that India's management saw the problem as well.
 The better lesson for India lies in preparation. Shashank's 40 off 11 shows what is possible on this surface, and the squad has a chance to recover when they take on UAE in their next match.
